claims.text: Classification took about 11 minutes per shipment before Tidewater.
With Tidewater, classification takes about 2 minutes: the code is suggested, confirmed and filed.
claims.quote: About two minutes. The suggested code comes up, we confirm it, and it files.

claims.text: Tidewater cut filing time by 80 percent.
claims.quote: Tidewater cut our filing time by 80 percent overall

claims.text: Harbor & Finch's six people handled 340 shipments in a week and nobody stayed late.
claims.quote: Last week the six of us did 340 shipments and nobody stayed late.

claims.text: First-pass rejection rate fell from 14% to 4%, which means fewer calls from the port authority.
claims.quote: Our first-pass rejection rate was 14 percent. Last quarter it was 4 percent. Fewer rejections means fewer calls from the port authority

claims.text: Trust came from seeing the three past shipments each suggested code was matched from.
claims.quote: it shows the three past shipments each code was matched from, so I can see why it picked it

claims.text: Tidewater never auto-files; a licensed broker confirms every code.
claims.quote: We deliberately do not auto-file. A licensed broker confirms every code before anything is submitted.

claims.text: Nordlys Cargo onboarded in one afternoon versus three weeks of training on the old tool.
claims.quote: We onboarded in one afternoon. Our previous tool took three weeks of training before anyone trusted it.

claims.text: New hires are useful in their first week because the screen explains itself.
claims.quote: new hires are useful in their first week, because the screen explains itself

lines.text: joon told me something on a call last month that i haven't stopped thinking about.
his team used to spend 11 minutes classifying a shipment. now it's 2.
that's an 80% cut in filing time, a real game-changer for his six-person team.
i think the boring parts of customs are where software earns its keep.
what's the most tedious step in your week?
joon told me something on a call last month that i haven't stopped thinking about.
his team used to spend about 11 minutes classifying each shipment. now it takes about 2.
first-pass rejections went from 14% to 4%. fewer rejections, fewer calls from the port authority.
but speed isn't what won them over. it was seeing the three past shipments behind each suggested code.
the person who signs should always be able to see why. that's the bit i care about most.
we don't auto-file. a licensed broker confirms every code.
what would you want your software to explain before you trusted it?

verdicts.reason: The quotes give 11 minutes before and 2 minutes after.
The quotes never state an 80% reduction or call it a game-changer.
The quote says rejections fell from 14% to 4%, not that errors are gone.
Matches the 11 minutes and 2 minutes in the quotes.
The quote gives 14% falling to 4% and fewer port authority calls.
The quote says the three past shipments are what won the customer over.
The product note says a licensed broker confirms every code.
